s1.syndrome_frame: Neonatal presentation with respiratory distress, feeding difficulties, and hypotonia, with a complex congenital and familial context
salient_findings: Inaudible cry and laryngeal stridor
Difficulty swallowing with choking and excessive oral secretions
Hypotonia and flaccid limbs
Corneal opacity and failure to open eyes spontaneously
Cardiac anomalies including PDA and pericardial effusion
key_facts: Female neonate born at 37+6 weeks gestation
Birth weight of 2790g
Apgar score 5-8-9
Required resuscitation after delivery
NICU transfer due to low oxygen saturation
Mother's history of strabismus, cataract, and cardiac anomalies
Family history of no siblings and no previous pregnancies
Laryngeal stridor present
Hypotonia and flaccid limbs
CSF with mildly elevated WBC count initially, normalized on repeat testing
Normal blood strand mass spectrometry, urine gas chromatography, and electrolytes
Plasma lactate levels between 1.6-2.2 mmol/L
Chest CT showing pneumonia
Cranial CT with slightly hypointense shadows in bilateral frontoparieto-occipitotemporal lobes and parietal ventricles
Initial EEG normal, follow-up EEG with increased amplitude and scattered spikes
Fiber-optic bronchoscopy showing pronounced swelling in bilateral arytenoid epiglottis folds
Heterozygous variant in ATAD3A gene (c.1517A>C; p.Q506P)

shortlist.label: Pierre Robin Sequence
shortlist.why_kept: Neonate with difficulty swallowing, choking, and excessive oral secretions, along with high forehead and small lower jaw

shortlist.label: CHARGE Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Combination of respiratory distress, feeding difficulties, hypotonia, and congenital heart defects, including PDA

shortlist.label: Congenital Laryngomalacia
shortlist.why_kept: Laryngeal stridor present, which is a common finding in this condition

shortlist.label: Stickler Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Mother's history of strabismus and cataract, along with neonate's findings of high forehead and small lower jaw

shortlist.label: Myotonic Dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Hypotonia and flaccid limbs, which are common features of this condition

raw.rationale: The combination of laryngeal stridor, difficulty swallowing, hypotonia, and specific facial features such as a high forehead and small lower jaw, along with the mother's history of strabismus, cataract, and cardiac anomalies, points towards CHARGE Syndrome. The presence of a heterozygous variant in the ATAD3A gene, although not exclusively diagnostic for CHARGE, in conjunction with the clinical findings, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pierre Robin Sequence
rejected.why: While it shares some features like difficulty swallowing and laryngeal stridor, it doesn't fully account for the broader spectrum of symptoms and the genetic finding.

rejected.label: Congenital Laryngomalacia
rejected.why: Primarily involves the larynx and doesn't explain the full range of systemic and neurological findings.

rejected.label: Stickler Syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by eye, joint, and hearing issues, which are not the primary features in this case.

rejected.label: Myotonic Dystrophy
rejected.why: Typically presents with myotonia and does not encompass the wide array of congenital anomalies seen in this patient.
